audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows gave the stage to Poppy or called it even while every matching why says Kled wins it — level 2 all-in, level 3 skirmish, levels 4-5 trades, the level-6 all-in and the first-item window. The header also called the lane EVEN at 6/10 on a 46.01% win rate over 213 games.
audit.why: Kled out-duels a pre-item Poppy: Bear Trap yanks from 800 range, Violent Tendencies is burst attack speed, and remount resets the all-in faster than Heroic Charge's 14s.
audit.corrected: Rows 2 through 6 flipped to Kled in matched full/content pairs with ratings rescaled; difficulty raised to TRICKY 7/10. Row 1 stays Skill and row 7 stays Poppy, matching the audited kled__poppy mirror.

audit.why: Four spikes present — levels 2-3, level 6, first item, late — and each names the right owner of that window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two places call Kled's grab a W ('his W dash grab', 'while his W grab is down'). The grab is Bear Trap on a Rope (Q) at 800 range on 11/10/9/8/7s; W is Violent Tendencies, four fast attacks off an auto reset; the dash is Jousting (E), 550 range on 13/12/11/10/9s. The page also never mentions that Chaaaaaaaarge!!! arrives with a shield.
audit.why: Waiting out a 'W grab' means waiting on the wrong cooldown, and committing into an unshielded-looking R loses the trade to a shield that is actually there.
audit.corrected: Grab named as Q with its real cooldown and range; W named as the auto-reset burst tell to step out of; W-Steadfast Presence pointed at Jousting and the Skaarl charge, the two things in his kit that actually are dashes; R's shield now stated as something to force out before you commit.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Bear Trap on a Rope and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 7/10. The lane is decided by how well you dodge Bear Trap on a Rope and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Kled carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7/10, Kled carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: W deletes his dash mid-flight — hold it like a parry. Only take the trade when Kled's Bear Trap on a Rope is down.
edits.after: W stops Jousting, his 550-range E dash, mid-flight. Do not trade until Bear Trap is down — 11s at rank 1.

edits.before: Keeper’s Verdict punts the fight’s biggest threat across the map. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Kled's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: His Skaarl charge arrives with a shield, so force it out before you commit. Your R is a fling to break his all-in, not a kill button.

edits.before: E-ing with no wall behind him — the wall-stun is the whole trade; the dash alone is a tickle.
edits.after: Violent Tendencies is four fast attacks off an auto reset — step out on the wind-up.

edits.before: With Q+E online you can E-stun him into a wall and Q the max-HP chunk, but only if he wastes his W dash grab first.
edits.after: With Q+E online you can E-stun him into a wall and Q the max-HP chunk — but only after his 800-range Bear Trap misses.

edits.before: Land E (Heroic Charge) into a wall for the stun, then Q for the max-HP chunk while his W grab is down
edits.after: Land E into a wall for the stun, then Q the max-HP chunk in the 11s while Bear Trap is down

edits.before: Hold W (Steadfast Presence) to ground and block his Skaarl R charge or his remount dash engage
edits.after: Hold W to stop Jousting, his 550-range E dash, or the Skaarl R charge — both are dashes

notes: Not asserted, consistent with the kled__poppy mirror note: Bear Trap's yank is a displacement and Keeper's Verdict is a channel, so the yank very likely cancels your R — but nothing in the kits confirms that a yank interrupts a channel, so I left it out rather than guess. It is the single highest-value line still missing from this matchup if someone can verify it. Also unfixable here: dosFull[2].t 'W-tank his autos' and dontsFull[1].t 'Let him remount' are both under 25 characters, so the applier skips them; the descriptions under them were generic filler and dontsFull[2].d is the only one I could repoint at a real interaction.
